Estimate decisions per session, context size, inference cost, batching and cache reuse. Telemetry volume equals events per viewing hour times hours times encoded event size, with replication and retention overhead.

High-cardinality diagnostics can cost more than expected. Sample deliberately while preserving critical denominators and financial evidence.

Unit economics

Build a transparent model: delivery, encoding, storage, compute, observability, DRM and partners, support and engineering operations. Content acquisition and production economics are outside a pure infrastructure bill but central to the company.

The second chart is a sensitivity model, not a vendor quote. Show which assumptions dominate and where more measurement is valuable. A single precise-looking total hides uncertainty.

Decision rule: buy commodity capabilities until measured scale, differentiation or contractual requirements justify ownership. Include on-call, certification and migration cost, not only a lower per-unit infrastructure price.

PART IX / Building and operating the company

64 Building the organization and delivery roadmap

Reference design. An end-to-end service requires media operations, rights, product, engineering, security, finance and support. A collection of microservices is not a company.

Own outcomes

Assign domain owners for catalog/rights, media publication, playback, delivery, membership, recommendations, data, live, ads and platform operations. Each owns APIs, invariants, objectives, on-call and recovery evidence.

Avoid a split where one team writes a service and an unrelated team owns every production consequence. Shared platforms provide capabilities, while product domains retain correctness.

Stage one: narrow VOD

Launch a small licensed catalog on a limited tested device set using managed encoding, storage, CDN and approved DRM. Prove membership, rights, publication, protected playback, support and reconciliation.

Use simple discovery and recommendations. Do not let model ambition delay a dependable Play path.

Stage two: scale and diversification

Add better media optimization, richer localization, more devices, data governance and controlled experiments. Introduce stronger isolation, automated recovery and infrastructure ownership only where measured needs justify it.

Expand ads, downloads or additional regions with their own contracts and test matrices rather than hidden flags in the original happy path.

Stage three: live and interactive

Live needs venue partnerships, rehearsals, continuous pipelines, peak capacity and event operations. Cloud gaming adds interactive compute and authoritative state. Treat these as new operating capabilities, not merely another catalog category.

Build versus buy

Evaluate managed CDN, DRM, encoding, payments, search and observability against strategic differentiation, cost and operational control. Open-source software reduces some implementation work but does not remove staffing and reliability obligations.

Budget migrations and exits. A vendor abstraction is useful only when it preserves necessary semantics and evidence.

Production acceptance

Require documented authority, ownership, security review, load evidence, recovery drills, device certification and support procedures. A working demo is not a launch gate.

Organizational exercise: an invalid subtitle release affects one region during a live event. Identify who may withdraw the release, who communicates, and which teams validate the correction. Ambiguous authority is itself a reliability defect.

PART IX / Building and operating the company

65 Worked VOD journey: corrected audio and a lost reply

Illustrative scenario. A member starts a film while a corrected audio release is being published. The session response is lost, and an older progress update arrives later.

Before Play

Release R17 contains validated video, audio and captions. A corrected audio track forms candidate R18 while reusing unchanged video by digest. Publication validates timeline and protected playback, then conditionally changes the active pointer.

The catalog may briefly show metadata from R17. That projection does not decide which release a new session pins.

Commit the session

The client sends intent K with capabilities and preferences. Playback resolves R18, evaluates rights and membership, and atomically creates session S, its stream lease, the idempotency result and an outbox event.

The response is lost. The client retries K with the same semantic payload. The server returns S, not a second lease. Reusing K with different profile or title conflicts.

Render and continue

The session contract points to compatible R18 media. The license service verifies the session and key mapping. The client fetches initialization and segments, then reports first frame.

Another viewer already using R17 remains pinned to that coherent release. The audio correction does not rewrite R17's cached URL or mix tracks midstream.

Resume ordering

The viewer reaches minute 50, rewinds to minute 20 and sends a newer sequence. A delayed minute-50 heartbeat arrives afterward. The generation/sequence rule rejects the older update, preserving the rewind.

An offline old device may contribute historical evidence but cannot overwrite the current resume owner without the defined policy.

Diagnose and close

Operators can link intent K, session S, release R18, license, source and client outcome. Outbox duplication produces no duplicate local downstream effect. Unreferenced candidate artifacts are eventually collected.

What the scenario proves conceptually: release publication, session admission and progress updates have different authorities and ordering rules. One global "latest timestamp wins" policy would be wrong for all three.

PART IX / Building and operating the company

66 Worked live incident: conflicting candidates and region loss

Illustrative scenario. Two encoders produce candidates for one segment while the origin's authoritative region fails after selection commits but before acknowledgment.

Establish the timeline

Event E uses generation G9. Segment identity includes G9, rendition and sequence 240. Candidate A and candidate B have different digests and provenance. Both may be technically decodable, but only one can define the immutable selected object.

Selection and uncertainty

The current writer at epoch 12 validates and selects A, commits its record and loses the reply during failure. The client or worker sees a timeout, not evidence that no selection occurred.

Recovery establishes epoch 13 through the chosen authority mechanism and fences epoch 12. It restores or reads durable selection evidence. Retrying A is idempotent. B conflicts at the same identity and cannot overwrite A merely because the response was lost.

Preserve serving and continuity

Replicated A can continue to be served from another location. Routing changes do not change byte identity. If A is unavailable everywhere, operators follow the documented gap or continuity policy rather than publishing B under the same cached URL without accounting for divergence.

Subsequent segments use the current authorized pipeline. Any generation change is explicit, with compatible manifest and decoder behavior.

Viewer and ad effects

The player may use buffered media while steering recovers. Measure stalls and live-edge drift, not just origin uptime. An ad break affected by the incident retains separate decision, delivery and observed-play evidence.

Do not count a planned or prefetched ad as completed because the origin recovered.

Reconcile

Compare selected segments, stored objects, candidate conflicts, writer epochs and client outcomes. Identify whether any content was never captured; no database restore can recreate that moment.

Key boundary: safe recovery restores authority and continuity evidence. It does not invent missing history or let whichever server restarts first decide the past.

PART IX / Building and operating the company

67 Incident runbooks and operational questions

Reference design. A runbook links a symptom to safe actions, authority and evidence. It is not an unbounded list of commands to try.

Playback-start regression

Confirm eligible intent denominator and affected cohorts. Split decision, license, fetch and decoder phases. Check recent client, media, policy and configuration releases. Mitigate the narrow cause: compatible fallback, targeted rollback or capacity protection. Do not bypass rights to improve a success metric.

Invalid media release

Identify release and affected tracks/devices. Stop new publication or withdraw the faulty pointer under approval. Validate the previous release before rollback; it may have expired rights. Preserve existing-session policy and publish a corrected immutable version.

Live source or timeline failure

Use the shared event timeline. Identify source, encoder, packaging or origin failure. Switch only to a validated compatible path or approved continuity behavior. Fence stale writers and preserve selected segment identities.

Regional authority loss

Declare uncertainty, establish new ownership through the documented mechanism, fence old writers, restore and replay. Validate release, session and external-effect consistency before broad reopening. Failback is a new controlled transition, not an automatic return to the original region.

Ad measurement discrepancy

Compare decisions, delivery, observations and accepted records. Quarantine conflicting identities, preserve late evidence and apply corrections through auditable adjustments. Do not directly edit aggregate totals to make dashboards match.

Telemetry blindness

Check ingestion lag, schema rejection, sampling and client reporting. Use independent synthetic probes and server evidence while acknowledging limited visibility. A drop in errors during telemetry loss is not recovery.

Each runbook needs owner, trigger, abort condition, privileges, expected effect, validation and communication. Rehearse it. A command that was safe last year can become dangerous after a schema or topology change.

PART IX / Building and operating the company

68 Production gates and the final architecture review

Reference design. The playbook is a design and learning reference, not a claim that a production Netflix equivalent has been built or certified.

Correctness gates

Prove scoped idempotency, conditional publication, stream admission, stale-writer rejection, progress ordering and consumer deduplication. Document where authority is unavailable under partition and what the user sees.

Check rights, key and release compatibility. Models and caches must not become accidental authority for permissions.

Experience gates

Measure first frame, stalls, decoder failures, accessibility and live-edge delay on representative devices and networks. Include unsupported and old firmware cohorts. Retain incomplete sessions in failure analysis.

A server load test cannot certify media playback or user interaction.

Reliability gates

Exercise the intended failure domain, cold recovery, replay and failback. Verify capacity after failure and rejection of old writers. Confirm that restored state does not repeat external effects or revive deleted authority.

Test overload with retries and shared dependencies. Demonstrate that optional work degrades before critical work collapses.

Security and operational gates

Complete threat modeling, access review, key lifecycle, privacy/retention, supply-chain controls and incident rehearsals. Approve support tools and high-impact operator actions.

Live and partner integrations need joint certification and clear escalation. Commercial rights and legal obligations require qualified review for the actual markets.

Evidence and limits

The companion's 42 local tests cover selected teaching properties in SQLite. They do not establish global consensus, DRM compliance, media quality, network performance, ad billability or completion of the 64-scenario catalog.

Before launch, replace illustrative targets, schemas and costs with measured and approved contracts. Keep dated public evidence separate from your own decisions.

The final question: for every important outcome, can the team name the authority, immutable evidence, expiry, failure behavior and recovery procedure? When the answer is clear, the architecture becomes operable rather than merely drawable.

A Logical data model and ownership

Reference design. This is an implementation map, not Netflix's private schema. Forty-two logical entities are grouped by authority. Physical placement can change without changing the meaning of the contracts. The executable lab deliberately implements only eleven small tables.

Forty-two entities

Entity Owner and key Important invariant
1. Account Membership; account_id Commercial identity is not a viewing profile
2. Profile Experience; profile_id Account ownership and deletion tombstone are explicit
3. Device registration Device trust; device_id Credentials, capability and risk are separate
4. Plan Membership; plan_id + revision Features and effective version are immutable evidence
5. Subscription Membership; subscription_id State follows approved effective-time transitions
6. Membership period Membership; account + interval Playback permission has a bounded effective window
7. Invoice Finance; invoice_id Issued financial history is not silently overwritten
8. Payment attempt Finance; operation_id External retries retain one durable provider reference
9. Adjustment Finance; adjustment_id Corrections refer to prior evidence rather than erase it
10. Work Catalog; work_id Editorial identity is distinct from an encoded object
11. Edition Catalog; edition_id A defined cut owns a presentation timeline
12. Rights grant Rights; grant_id + revision Territory, use and effective interval are explicit
13. Partner submission Media supply; submission_id Replacement bytes create a new submission
14. Composition Media supply; composition_digest Referenced essence and timeline are resolvable
15. Source asset Media supply; content_digest Immutable bytes and custody evidence agree
16. Workflow instance Orchestration; workflow_id Durable state survives worker replacement
17. Task attempt Orchestration; task_id + attempt Late attempts cannot overwrite a selected result
18. Rendition Media; rendition_id Codec and timing requirements are precise
19. Localized track Localization; track_id Locale, role and edition compatibility are explicit
20. Quality assessment Media quality; artifact + rule version Approval evidence refers to exact bytes and checks
21. Key reference Content security; key_id Registry stores references, not broadly readable keys
22. Release manifest Publication; release_id Required dependency graph is immutable and validated
23. Active release pointer Publication; title + territory scope Conditional revision update chooses one release
24. Artwork asset Creative; asset_id Editorial approval precedes personalized selection
25. Embedding artifact ML platform; entity + model digest Vector space is a semantic type, not only a dimension
26. Playback intent Playback; principal + idempotency key Same key binds one canonical semantic payload
27. Playback session Playback; session_id Pins release, policy, device and authority expiry
28. Stream lease Playback admission; lease_id Competing allocation is authoritative and bounded
29. License transaction Content security; license_request_id Requested keys belong to permitted content and device
30. Progress generation History; profile + edition Only an authorized current generation owns resume writes
31. Progress event History; generation + sequence Rewinds survive; stale sequence cannot move current state
32. Download record Offline client; device + release Bytes and persistent permission have separate readiness
33. Appliance inventory Delivery; appliance + object digest Desired placement differs from verified physical content
34. Placement plan Delivery control; plan_id + revision Storage, fill bandwidth and launch deadlines are bounded
35. Live event generation Live control; event + generation Rehearsal and restart namespaces do not collide
36. Live segment candidate Live origin; key + attempt Provenance, timing and digest precede selection
37. Selected live segment Live origin; event + generation + rendition + sequence One immutable digest wins per identity
38. Ad opportunity Advertising; opportunity_id Timeline and eligibility are distinct from ad selection
39. Ad decision Advertising; decision_id Selected creative must be feasible and policy-compliant
40. Ad observation Measurement; event_id Replays deduplicate; conflicting identity is quarantined
41. Experiment exposure Experimentation; exposure_id Actual treatment differs from server assignment
42. Outbox event Owning domain; event_id Fact and local publication intent commit atomically

Physical schema choices

Use opaque primary keys and explicit revisions. Index according to access patterns, not every field. Session admission needs efficient active-lease lookup by account and expiry. Release publication needs a small conditional pointer and immutable candidate records. Live selection needs uniqueness on the complete segment identity. Progress needs conditional generation and sequence access.

Money uses integer minor units and explicit currency. Timestamps record effective time, observation time and receipt time when those differ. Do not use one ambiguous updated_at column as the ordering authority for every domain.

Foreign keys are useful within one database. Across service boundaries, immutable references, validation and reconciliation replace the illusion of a distributed foreign-key transaction. Deletion is often a tombstone workflow rather than immediate physical cascade.

The lab's SQLite schema uses transactions and uniqueness to demonstrate local invariants. A production implementation must add authentication, authorization, encryption, migrations, replication, recovery, connection management and workload isolation. No table list proves those properties.

Partition and retention review

For each entity, document tenant or account scope, hot-key risk, retention purpose, deletion behavior, backup policy and reconstruction source. A projection can be rebuilt from authority; an authoritative financial record cannot be casually discarded because its cache can be warmed.

Do not partition all live events by one global row. Conversely, splitting one concurrency invariant across independent shards without a coordination protocol loses the invariant. Partition boundaries follow the write contract before the throughput target.

IMPLEMENTATION APPENDICES

B Twelve proposed API contracts

Reference design. Paths are illustrative and are not Netflix APIs. Every write derives its principal from verified credentials, not from an untrusted body field. Error classes are stable machine-readable values. The client-visible timeout model is explicitly "outcome may be unknown."

Common envelope

A request has request_id, deadline and authenticated actor. Consequential operations may require Idempotency-Key, expected_revision and an internally verified writer_epoch. Canonical payload hashing excludes transport-only fields but includes every semantic input that changes the result. The canonicalization version is part of the contract.

Responses distinguish validation failure, policy denial, conflict, overload, unavailable authority and unknown outcome. A retryable error does not mean a caller should create a new operation identity. Return a status URL or lookup key for durable intent.

Contract Input and authority Result and important behavior
1. GET /catalog Profile, locale, query cursor Versioned projection; not playback permission
2. POST /search Query, locale, context, approved filters Grounded catalog IDs; eligible retrieval with final playback check
3. POST /playback/intents Title, device capabilities, tracks; idempotency key One session result or explicit state; duplicates do not consume another slot
4. GET /playback/intents/{key} Same verified principal and operation scope Resolves lost replies; does not renew expiry
5. POST /sessions/{id}/renew Session, expected lease revision, current authority Bounded renewed contract or denial; separate from create replay
6. POST /progress Session generation, sequence, position Accepted, duplicate, stale or conflict; rewind is valid
7. POST /downloads Release, tracks, device and eligibility Durable preparation state; ready requires media and permission
8. POST /media/submissions Project, composition and object references Quarantined immutable submission; upload is not acceptance
9. POST /releases/{id}/publish Expected pointer revision and approved evidence Conditional pointer commit plus outbox; stale publisher conflicts
10. PUT /live/{event}/{generation}/segments/{key} Candidate digest, provenance, validation, writer epoch Select once; different bytes at the same identity conflict
11. POST /ad-observations Event, opportunity, decision, creative, observed state Durable receipt; duplicates harmless, conflicts quarantined
12. POST /membership/changes Plan/action, effective time and operation key Audited transition; provider uncertainty is reconciled

Session creation example

{
  "title_id": "work_7",
  "profile_id": "profile_2",
  "device_id": "device_8",
  "capability_revision": "cap_19",
  "preferred_audio": "en",
  "preferred_text_role": "captions",
  "resume_context": {"edition_id": "edit_4"}
}

The server derives account ownership, validates profile access and resolves an approved immutable release. The durable result contains session_id, release_id, policy_revision, lease expiry and references to the permitted manifest and licensing workflow. It does not expose raw content keys or accept a caller-supplied "is_paid" flag.

A replay after expiry returns the historical result or a documented expired status; it does not extend the lease. New viewing intent or renewal must be explicit. The distinction prevents a retained idempotency key from becoming unlimited access.

Conditional publication example

POST /releases/release_18/publish
If-Match: pointer-revision-17
Idempotency-Key: publish-release-18

candidate_digest = verified immutable graph digest
required_evidence = quality, localization, protected-playback, delivery
rights_revision = independently validated current grant revision

The publication authority validates the current writer epoch and expected pointer revision at commit. A successful response proves selection of the candidate, not that every global cache has already refreshed. New sessions use the selected release according to propagation policy.

Authentication and signature boundaries

Use approved platform and DRM protocols for licensing. For ordinary service webhooks, signatures cover the exact received bytes and relevant timestamp/identifier fields under a documented canonicalization rule. Constant-time comparison prevents trivial timing leakage, but replay prevention still needs durable identity and an accepted time window. A valid signature does not authorize arbitrary state transitions.

Never log raw credentials, keys or full signed URLs unnecessarily. Redact secrets while retaining operation identity and validation outcome. Rotating a signing key requires a bounded overlap strategy and clear key identifiers.

Compatibility gates

Test missing optional fields, unknown enums, old client behavior, duplicate requests, payload conflicts, stale revisions, deadline expiry and response loss after commit. API documentation is incomplete until it says which result is authoritative when the caller sees no response.

IMPLEMENTATION APPENDICES

C Eight critical algorithms

Reference design. These algorithms state boundaries rather than pretending that a few lines implement a globally distributed streaming company. Production versions require the storage and authority properties described in the chapters.

C1. Idempotent session admission

create_session(principal, key, payload, current_epoch):
  digest = canonical_hash(payload)
  begin authoritative transaction
    assert current_epoch is still authorized
    existing = lookup(principal, CREATE_SESSION, key)
    if existing:
      assert existing.payload_digest == digest
      return original_result_without_extending_expiry(existing)
    validate account/profile ownership and policy versions
    expire or ignore leases according to authoritative time
    assert active_lease_count < effective_stream_limit
    session = create pinned release + bounded lease
    insert unique idempotency result
    append outbox SESSION_CREATED
  commit
  return session

The transaction must serialize competing admissions for the same invariant. Counting on a stale replica and then inserting on another writer does not enforce the limit. Remote policy preparation occurs before the transaction, with required versions validated at commit or through a reservation protocol.

The caller can lose the reply after commit. Lookup resolves the result. No second stream is allocated merely because the first acknowledgment disappeared.

C2. Conditional release publication

publish(candidate, expected_pointer_revision, epoch):
  verify candidate graph and required evidence
  begin authoritative transaction
    assert epoch is current
    assert candidate is READY and still eligible
    pointer = read current pointer for scope
    assert pointer.revision == expected_pointer_revision
    update pointer to candidate with revision + 1
    append outbox RELEASE_PUBLISHED
  commit

Large artifacts are already immutable and validated. The atomic part is selection, not copying every byte. Evidence depending on mutable rights or configuration must still be valid at commit. A previous release is not automatically a safe rollback target.

C3. Resume ordering that preserves rewind

apply_progress(profile, edition, generation, sequence, position):
  begin local authoritative transaction
    state = read progress owner
    if generation != state.current_generation: return STALE_GENERATION
    if sequence < state.sequence: return STALE_SEQUENCE
    if sequence == state.sequence:
      assert position and semantic payload match stored event
      return DUPLICATE
    update sequence and position, even when position decreases
  commit

Generations are server-issued and authorized. Clients cannot invent a larger generation to seize ownership. A position maximum is incorrect because rewinds and rewatching are valid. Device wall clocks do not replace this ordering contract.

C4. Immutable live-segment selection

select_segment(key, candidate, epoch):
  assert candidate has valid timing, digest and required approval
  begin authoritative transaction
    assert epoch is current and generation is active
    existing = lookup full segment key
    if existing:
      if existing.digest == candidate.digest: return DUPLICATE
      raise IMMUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONFLICT
    insert selected candidate and provenance
    append outbox SEGMENT_SELECTED
  commit

The key includes event generation and rendition. A stale writer cannot publish merely because its process is still running. Byte replacement under an already cached identity is prohibited even when the replacement looks preferable.

C5. Consumer effect with durable receipt

consume(event):
  begin consumer transaction
    receipt = lookup event_id
    if receipt:
      assert receipt.digest == canonical_hash(event)
      return DUPLICATE
    apply local domain effect under revision rules
    insert event receipt with digest
  commit
  advance transport checkpoint

Checkpointing before the local transaction risks lost effects. Committing first permits duplicate delivery, which the receipt handles. An external side effect needs its own idempotent operation and reconciliation; the local transaction cannot control an unrelated system atomically.

C6. Conservative bitrate selection

choose_rendition(compatible, estimate, buffer_seconds):
  assert inputs are finite and nonnegative
  budget = estimate * safety_factor
  candidates = compatible with bitrate <= budget
  choice = best approved candidate, or lowest compatible fallback
  if buffer is low: cap upward movement or choose safer rung
  apply hysteresis and device/decoder constraints
  return choice

This is a teaching baseline, not Netflix's player algorithm. Real controllers use segment sizes, transport behavior, decoder signals, startup phase and live latency. Evaluate complete traces: high average quality can conceal severe stalls.

C7. Regional writer handoff

handoff(old_epoch, recovery_evidence):
  stop or restrict new consequential admissions
  acquire new authority through the chosen consensus/ownership system
  advance epoch conditionally
  ensure all durable write boundaries reject old epochs
  restore and replay committed state
  reconcile immutable objects and external references
  validate invariants and reopen in stages

A local counter is not a global ownership protocol. The teaching lab checks an epoch stored in one SQLite database; it does not implement distributed consensus. Existing media delivery can continue only within retained token and license bounds.

C8. Ad-observation receipt and correction

record_observation(event_id, semantic_payload):
  digest = canonical_hash(semantic_payload)
  begin measurement transaction
    prior = lookup event_id
    if prior:
      assert prior.digest == digest
      return DUPLICATE
    validate source and plausible identity relationships
    insert observation with acceptance status and evidence
  commit
  reconcile with decision and delivery views

The durable receipt proves a narrow uniqueness property, not that a human watched the ad or that a contract permits billing. Later evidence creates an auditable correction rather than a silent historical rewrite.

E Service contracts, freshness and recovery

Reference design. Values below are categories and review questions, not contractual Netflix guarantees. Each production team must set and measure its own numeric objectives.

Service/domain Authoritative commitment Acceptable degradation Recovery proof
Catalog projection Accurate versioned display data Reduced or bounded stale browsing Rebuilt projection matches source checkpoints
Rights Effective grant and restriction No new authority when required facts unknown Current revisions and takedown propagation verified
Membership Effective commercial entitlement Explicit approved grace only Provider references and periods reconciled
Playback admission One bounded session/lease per intent Lookup or unavailable result Idempotency, quota and epoch invariants hold
Licensing Permitted keys under device policy Approved renewal behavior only Key mapping, expiry and security checks pass
Publication One selected coherent release Pause new publication Pointer, evidence and objects agree
Media delivery Correct immutable bytes Alternate source or approved quality reduction Reachability, digest and capacity verified
Live origin Immutable segment selection Approved continuity behavior Generation, epoch and timeline reconciled
Progress Current authorized resume state Delay noncritical propagation Stale generations cannot overwrite
Recommendation Eligible useful ranking Simple approved baseline Model/feature versions and coverage restored
Measurement Durable attributable evidence Delayed provisional reporting Decisions, observations and corrections reconcile
Analytics Defined snapshot and semantics Visible freshness delay Completeness and lineage checks pass

Freshness is a policy, not a cache setting

For each read, specify what happens when the version is too old. Recommendations can often use older features. Rights for new playback may require current authority. A deleted profile must not be revived by a long-lived cache. The correct TTL follows the business risk, not a generic performance convention.

Use stale-while-revalidate only where stale data is permitted. A successful refresh request is not proof that every consumer has adopted the new version. Measure propagation and retain evidence for urgent revocation.

Recovery time decomposition

Total recovery includes detection, decision, ownership/fencing, restoration, replay, validation, traffic reopening and user recovery. Quoting only database restore time understates the service outage. Failback can have the same classes of risk.

Recovery point describes possible lost committed data under the specified failure. It is not automatically zero because there are multiple replicas. Clarify whether acknowledgments require remote durability and what happens when that path is unavailable.

Dependency contracts

For every critical call, record deadline, retry owner, maximum attempts, concurrency, idempotency, fallback and security context. Dependency fan-out should be visible in design review. A service objective that ignores required downstream services is not an end-to-end objective.

Grace and revocation

Grace preserves previously granted authority under a bounded explicit policy. It does not invent new permission or bypass denied rights. Offline licenses are a form of previously granted bounded capability; their revocation limits must be accepted before launch.

Immutable media and release graphs Safe caching, reproducibility and correction Retained versions consume storage and need collection
Conditional active pointers Small atomic publication boundary Readiness and rights must be validated separately
Scoped idempotency Lost replies do not duplicate effects Retention, canonicalization and lookup must be defined
One authority per consequential invariant Clear concurrency semantics May reduce availability during partition
Transactional outbox Local state and event intent agree Delivery duplicates and consumer receipts remain necessary
Server-issued progress generations Preserves rewind and rejects stale devices Overlapping-session policy needs product ownership
Versioned feature namespaces Safe model/embedding migration Backfills and dual storage add cost
Managed CDN/DRM early Faster certified initial delivery Vendor constraints and exit strategy require review
Separate live resource pools Protects deadlines from backfills Reserved capacity can reduce utilization
Deterministic policy outside models Scores cannot grant forbidden authority Policy maintenance remains an explicit responsibility
Staged device-aware releases Contains cohort-specific failures Requires representative hardware and telemetry

Stage gates rather than calendar promises

Foundation stage: approved content and rights, a small device matrix, membership, immutable release publication, protected playback and support. Demonstrate the full journey and basic recovery before adding product breadth.

Reliability stage: measured service objectives, outboxes and reconciliation, overload control, authority fencing, tested backup/restore, security and privacy processes. Replace illustrative targets with actual evidence.

Scale stage: workload-driven partitioning, better media optimization, personalization, governed analytics and capacity economics. Adopt specialized infrastructure when the measured benefit exceeds operational cost.

Diversification stage: ads, downloads, live and games each receive independent contracts, failure tests and operational owners. Do not assume that success in VOD transfers automatically.

Build-versus-buy worksheet

Evaluate differentiation, compliance, latency, cost at forecast volume, operational staffing, certification, vendor lock-in, migration and failure evidence. A lower unit price can be outweighed by hardware support, 24-hour operations and difficult recovery.

For any internal replacement, define the old and new authority, migration checkpoints, comparison metrics, rollback condition and retained evidence. A rewrite is not complete when it serves traffic; it is complete when correctness and operations survive the transition.

Definition of done

A service has an owner, reviewed invariant, API/error contract, schema/migration path, security controls, observability, load evidence, recovery drill, support procedure and documented limits. These are deliverables, not optional paperwork after implementation.

IMPLEMENTATION APPENDICES

G Glossary: sixty-six terms

Term Meaning in this playbook
1. ABR Adaptive bitrate selection by the player under network and buffer constraints
2. Account Commercial identity owning membership and billing
3. Ad opportunity A defined chance to present an advertisement on a timeline
4. Ad observation Evidence reported about actual ad playback, distinct from selection
5. Admission control Decision to accept work before resources or invariants are exhausted
6. Artifact digest Cryptographic identity of immutable bytes
7. Authority The component and protocol permitted to commit a particular fact
8. Availability zone A provider failure-domain concept whose actual dependencies need review
9. Backfill Reprocessing a historical interval under a specified code/data version
10. Bounded grace Explicit temporary preservation of prior permission under defined limits
11. Buffer Media already available for future playback, usually measured in seconds
12. Bulkhead Resource isolation preventing one workload from exhausting all others
13. Canary Limited rollout used to observe risk before wider deployment
14. Capability tuple Precise codec, security, display and decode requirements of a device
15. Catalog projection Read-optimized view of titles and metadata, not final playback authority
16. CDN Content delivery network serving objects near or efficiently to users
17. Checkpoint Recorded processing position; not automatically a business transaction
18. Composition A specified media timeline referencing source components
19. Conditional write Update accepted only when an expected revision or condition still holds
20. Content key Secret used for media encryption/decryption under an approved key system
21. Control plane Services deciding configuration, authority and coordination
22. Contribution Transport of live source media into the processing pipeline
23. Data plane Path carrying media or other bulk useful payloads
24. Deadline Latest time at which an operation can complete usefully
25. Decoder Component converting encoded media into renderable samples
26. Delivery token Bounded authorization to retrieve specified media resources
27. DRM Digital rights management enforcing approved content-use restrictions
28. Edition A particular editorial cut with a defined timeline
29. EME Encrypted Media Extensions, a browser interface to key systems
30. Embedding Learned representation whose model and preprocessing define its meaning
31. Entitlement Effective commercial/policy permission, separate from a DRM license
32. Epoch Monotonic authority generation used to reject stale writers
33. Error budget Permitted failure under a precisely defined service objective
34. Exposure Actual application of an experiment treatment, not mere assignment
35. Fencing Rejection of operations from an obsolete owner at the durable boundary
36. Fill Prepositioning content at a serving location
37. First frame First rendered video frame observed by the client
38. Generation Explicit namespace for a session, progress owner or live timeline
39. HDR High dynamic range; requires compatible mastering, signaling and display
40. Idempotency Repeating one logical operation preserves its defined effect
41. IMF Interoperable Master Format for component-based mastering/interchange
42. Invariant A condition that must remain true across allowed operations
43. Key system Approved implementation handling protected media licenses and keys
44. Ladder Set of encoded representations available for adaptation
45. Lease Time-bounded reservation or authority requiring explicit renewal
46. Live edge Most recent useful point in the live presentation timeline
47. Manifest Contract describing media, timing, compatibility and locations
48. MSE Media Source Extensions for browser-controlled media buffering
49. Outbox Event intent committed atomically with local authoritative state
50. Per-shot encoding Allocation of encoding choices according to scene/shot complexity
51. Profile Personal experience and preference identity within an account
52. QoE Quality of experience, measured from user-visible playback outcomes
53. Rebuffering Playback interruption caused by insufficient usable buffered media
54. Release Immutable approved combination of compatible media and metadata
55. Rendition One encoded representation with precise technical requirements
56. Rights window Effective interval and scope of permitted content use
57. RPO Recovery point objective: acceptable loss bound under a defined failure
58. RTO Recovery time objective for a defined restored service condition
59. Segment Addressable media unit on a presentation timeline
60. Session Bounded playback contract binding user, device, release and policy
61. SLI Service-level indicator: the actual defined measurement
62. SLO Service-level objective: a target for an indicator
63. SLA Contractual service agreement, not interchangeable with an internal target
64. Tombstone Durable deletion/revocation marker preventing stale resurrection
65. VBR Variable bitrate, with demand changing across content intervals
66. VMAF Netflix-origin perceptual quality tooling with model/setup-dependent scores

Reading the implementation companion

Run the standard-library test suite in the code directory. It creates temporary local databases and exercises deterministic and concurrent cases. The output is a local execution report. Read the schema and transaction boundaries alongside the tests; a passing test proves only its asserted property under that implementation and environment.

The broader architecture requires additional distributed, media, security, device, load and partner evidence. Keep those limits visible when adapting the teaching code into a real service.
